sentences.en: Suheila Hashimi was 23 years old when we first met, but we almost didn't.
sentences.zh: 我们初次见面时，苏海拉·哈希米才23岁，但我们差点就没能见成。

sentences.en: She was so shy, I thought she might cancel our first interview.
sentences.zh: 她太害羞了，我以为她可能会取消我们的第一次采访。

sentences.en: It was February in Providence, Rhode Island.
sentences.zh: 那是二月的罗德岛州普罗维登斯。

sentences.en: Brown University's campus was covered in about a foot of snow.
sentences.zh: 布朗大学的校园覆盖着大约一英尺厚的积雪。

sentences.en: I met Suheila at the student center.
sentences.zh: 我在学生中心见到了苏海拉。

sentences.en: We talked for so long that she invited me to dinner.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了很久，她邀请我一起吃晚饭。

sentences.en: It was around 7.30 and the dining halls were jammed with students standing in long lines.
sentences.zh: 当时大约7点半，食堂里挤满了排着长队的学生。

sentences.en: Since she got to Brown, Suheila had been struggling to find things she could eat.
sentences.zh: 自从来到布朗大学，苏海拉就一直在为找不到能吃的东西而苦恼。

sentences.en: So she stuck to her usual, which was cheese, pizza, and salad.
sentences.zh: 所以她坚持吃她惯常的食物，也就是奶酪、披萨和沙拉。

sentences.en: She joked that at least the dining halls offered ice cream.
sentences.zh: 她开玩笑说，至少食堂还提供冰淇淋。

sentences.en: Suheila told me how much she missed her mother's cooking, especially her mother's cobbly palau, the steamed rice, the carrots, the raisins,
sentences.zh: 苏海拉告诉我她有多想念母亲做的饭菜，尤其是母亲做的抓饭，那些蒸米饭、胡萝卜、葡萄干、

sentences.en: and meat, and just how inedible the food on campus felt to her.
sentences.zh: 还有肉，以及她觉得校园里的食物有多难以下咽。

sentences.en: Suheila is an Afghan refugee who fled Kabul last summer.
sentences.zh: 苏海拉是一位阿富汗难民，去年夏天逃离了喀布尔。

sentences.en: She got to Brown around Christmas, right before the next semester started, and decided
sentences.zh: 她在圣诞节前后，也就是下学期开始前不久来到布朗大学，并决定

sentences.en: to take mostly philosophy classes, thinking they could help her process this whole transition into a sudden new life as a university student in America.
sentences.zh: 主要修读哲学课程，她认为这些课程可以帮助她处理这种突然转变为美国大学生的新生活。

sentences.en: I remember she told me she was feeling numb and was having a hard time connecting with many of the other students.
sentences.zh: 我记得她告诉我，她感到麻木，很难与其他许多学生建立联系。

sentences.en: She said she was basically just surviving.
sentences.zh: 她说她基本上只是在生存。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Suheila's family was still trapped in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，苏海拉的家人仍被困在阿富汗。

sentences.en: Her mother had health issues and trouble walking, and Suheila constantly stressed about their safety.
sentences.zh: 她母亲有健康问题，走路困难，苏海拉一直为他们的安全感到焦虑。

sentences.en: I had heard about an effort to rescue a group of 150 young Afghan women out of the country after it fell to the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 我听说在阿富汗落入塔利班之手后，有人努力营救了一群150名年轻的阿富汗女性。

sentences.en: They were all students or alumni of the Asian University for Women.
sentences.zh: 她们都是亚洲女子大学的学生或校友。

sentences.en: Suheila was one of them.
sentences.zh: 苏海拉就是其中之一。

sentences.en: And then her mother came into her room and broke the news.

sentences.zh: 苏海拉记得她当时害怕得吃不下饭。

sentences.zh: 而她母亲只是说，如果塔利班要杀你，你不如先自杀。吃点东西吧。

sentences.en: Then they hugged for a long time.
sentences.zh: 然后她们拥抱了很久。

sentences.en: Not since the Vietnam War has there been an evacuation of civilians as large as what we saw last year in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 自越战以来，还没有哪次平民撤离行动像去年我们在阿富汗看到的那样大规模。

sentences.en: Starting last summer, an emergency action called Operation Allies Welcome brought more than 70,000 Afghan refugees to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 从去年夏天开始，一项名为“盟友欢迎行动”的紧急行动将超过7万名阿富汗难民带到了美国。

sentences.en: In the situation that Suheila and many other Afghan women like her found themselves, we see what it looks like to be the collateral damage of major foreign powers' decisions.
sentences.zh: 在苏海拉和许多像她一样的阿富汗女性所处的境遇中，我们看到了大国决策所带来的附带损害是什么样子。

sentences.en: In the decades-long war in Afghanistan, the country's 20 million or so women have always had the most to lose.
sentences.zh: 在阿富汗长达数十年的战争中，该国约2000万女性总是损失最惨重的一方。

sentences.zh: 在我访问布朗大学期间，哈希米（Hashemi）正面临着她“知识与现实”课程的一篇哲学论文截止日期。

sentences.en: She was writing about Descartes meditations, and she had questions about it.
sentences.zh: 她正在写关于笛卡尔《沉思录》的内容，对此她有一些疑问。

sentences.en: I went with her to meet her instructor, a graduate student whose office was in a corner of the philosophy department,
sentences.zh: 我和她一起去见她的导师，那是一位研究生，办公室在哲学系的一个角落里，

sentences.en: a small brick building with carpeted floors and narrow corridors.
sentences.zh: 那是一栋铺着地毯、走廊狭窄的砖砌小楼。

sentences.en: I need help with meditations one and two, she told her teacher, her voice barely above a whisper.
sentences.zh: “我需要关于第一和第二沉思的帮助，”她对老师说，声音几乎低不可闻。

sentences.en: From his point of view, nothing is certain and everything is doubtful.
sentences.zh: “从他的观点来看，没有什么东西是确定的，一切都是可疑的。”

sentences.en: Well, so what's his argument?
sentences.zh: “那么，他的论点是什么？”

sentences.en: It was hard for Hashemi to always stay focused on her studies, even though the brick buildings and the campus, which is partly enclosed by a wrought iron fence,
sentences.zh: 哈希米很难一直专注于学业，尽管那些砖砌建筑和部分被锻铁栅栏围起来的校园，

sentences.en: made Brown feel like the safest place in the world for her.
sentences.zh: 让布朗大学对她来说感觉像是世界上最安全的地方。

sentences.en: Her reading was regularly interrupted by disturbing calls from her family about a new person missing, or about the country's impending famine, or about another explosion.
sentences.zh: 她的阅读经常被家人打来的令人不安的电话所打断，内容是关于又有新人失踪、国家即将面临饥荒，或是又发生了爆炸。

sentences.en: There seemed to be no end in sight for the bad news from Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 来自阿富汗的坏消息似乎永无止境。

sentences.en: Sometimes my mind is saying, all you have are problems, only problems, Hashemi told me one evening.
sentences.zh: “有时我的大脑在说，你拥有的只有问题，只有问题，”哈希米一天晚上告诉我。

sentences.en: Most of her family was still trapped in Kabul, and her mother had health issues that made it difficult for her to walk.
sentences.zh: 她的家人大多仍被困在喀布尔，她的母亲有健康问题，走路都很困难。

sentences.en: Her helplessness here ate at her constantly.
sentences.zh: 在这里的无助感不断地折磨着她。

sentences.en: In her philosophy classes, she could be inconspicuous, listening to lectures and quietly taking notes.
sentences.zh: 在哲学课上，她可以保持低调，听讲座并安静地做笔记。

sentences.en: And like most of the other AUW women, she spent much of her time studying in her room or in the library, keeping a low profile.
sentences.zh: 像大多数其他亚洲女子大学的女性一样，她大部分时间都在房间或图书馆里学习，保持低调。

sentences.en: But so many people on campus seemed so eager to talk.
sentences.zh: 但校园里有太多人似乎非常渴望交谈。

sentences.en: I'd just be waiting, like, please don't ask me where I'm from, she said.
sentences.zh: “我只会等着，心想，求求你别问我来自哪里，”她说。

sentences.en: It was a bit hard for me to tell them I'm from Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 告诉他们我来自阿富汗对我来说有点困难。

sentences.en: Students often had misconceptions about what Afghan women were capable of, she felt.
sentences.zh: 她觉得，学生们经常对阿富汗女性的能力有误解。

sentences.en: They frequently seemed shocked to find out that Afghan women could travel abroad, or speak English, or go to universities.
sentences.zh: 他们经常对发现阿富汗女性可以出国、说英语或上大学感到震惊。

sentences.en: She described to me one incident when she was having her regular breakfast of bagel and butter, her buttered naan, she joked, with a few other Afghan women at a brown cafeteria.
sentences.zh: 她向我描述了一次经历，当时她正在布朗大学的食堂和几位阿富汗女性吃着她平时的早餐——百吉饼配黄油，她开玩笑说是“黄油馕”。

sentences.en: A group of boys sat at their table and asked where they were from.
sentences.zh: 一群男生坐在她们桌旁，问她们来自哪里。

sentences.en: Afghanistan, Hashemi said.
sentences.zh: “阿富汗，”哈希米说。

sentences.en: The boys got up and moved to another table.
sentences.zh: 男生们起身换到了另一张桌子。

sentences.en: Hashemi, angry, called her mother afterward.
sentences.zh: 哈希米很生气，事后给母亲打了电话。

sentences.en: This is not going to be a good country for me, because people are judging me, she said.
sentences.zh: “这对我不算是一个好国家，因为人们在评判我，”她说。

sentences.en: She felt depressed for almost a week, though she later acknowledged that she wasn't sure why they switched seats.
sentences.zh: 她抑郁了近一个星期，尽管她后来承认，她也不确定他们为什么要换座位。

sentences.en: She found it difficult to relate to other students, who, by the time of my midwinter visit, were already making plans for their spring breaks.
sentences.zh: 她发现很难与同学们产生共鸣，因为在我仲冬访问时，他们已经开始计划春假了。

sentences.en: My classmates here, they are thinking about where to go for the next vacation or holiday or weekend, and I'm thinking, how can I get a job to help my family?
sentences.zh: “这里的同学们在想下一个假期、节日或周末去哪里，而我在想，我怎么才能找到一份工作来帮助我的家人？”

sentences.en: As the semester advanced, the women began getting troubling updates from back home.
sentences.zh: 随着学期推进，这些女性开始收到来自家乡的令人不安的消息。

sentences.en: The Taliban were going after perceived enemies and imposing restrictions on women.
sentences.zh: 塔利班正在追捕他们眼中的敌人，并对女性施加限制。

sentences.en: According to witnesses cited in a report from Human Rights Watch, the Taliban were searching office buildings, collecting computers,
sentences.zh: 根据人权观察组织报告中引用的证人说法，塔利班正在搜查办公楼，没收电脑，

sentences.en: and tracking down women who work for the foreigners.
sentences.zh: 并追踪那些为外国人工作的女性。

sentences.en: Every AUW student I spoke to felt a deep fear for her family back home.
sentences.zh: 我采访的每一位亚洲女子大学的学生都为家乡的亲人感到深深的恐惧。

sentences.en: More than once, I spent hours interviewing someone, only to have her withdraw access a few days later, fearing some unknowable consequence.
sentences.zh: 不止一次，我花了几个小时采访某人，结果几天后她就拒绝了进一步交流，因为担心某种不可预知的后果。

sentences.en: Many declined to speak to me at all.
sentences.zh: 许多人完全拒绝与我交谈。

sentences.en: One student, who wished to remain anonymous, told me that her sibling had been a member of Afghan intelligence.
sentences.zh: 一名希望保持匿名的学生告诉我，她的兄弟姐妹曾是阿富汗情报部门的成员。

sentences.en: Now that sibling was in hiding, changing locations every few weeks, because the Taliban were hunting down anyone who had worked for the Afghan security forces.
sentences.zh: 现在那个兄弟姐妹正在躲藏，每隔几周就更换地点，因为塔利班正在搜捕任何曾为阿富汗安全部队工作过的人。

sentences.en: The woman's father, fearing for their safety, wouldn't let her younger sisters leave their house.
sentences.zh: 这位女性的父亲担心她们的安全，不让年幼的妹妹们离开家门。

sentences.en: I can't get it out of my mind, the woman told me, fighting back tears.
sentences.zh: “我无法把它从脑海中抹去，”这位女性强忍着泪水告诉我。

sentences.en: I can't find anyone to support my family.
sentences.zh: “我找不到任何人来支持我的家庭。”

sentences.en: The situation in Afghanistan is so much worse.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗的情况要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: Another student,
sentences.zh: 另一名学生，

sentences.en: Fariba Sarwari, a 19-year-old student at Suffolk University, told me that every night for months after she got to Boston, she lay in bed, gripped with loneliness,
sentences.zh: 法里巴·萨瓦里（Fariba Sarwari），萨福克大学的一名19岁学生告诉我，自从来到波士顿后，有几个月的时间，她每晚躺在床上，被孤独感笼罩，

sentences.en: listening to songs from Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 听着来自阿富汗的歌曲。

sentences.en: I just feel so bad.
sentences.zh: “我感觉太糟糕了。”

sentences.en: Why did this happen to my country?
sentences.zh: “为什么我的国家会发生这种事？”

sentences.en: For these young women who came of age in the early 2000s, in a relatively liberalized country, this was not a return to older ways of life.
sentences.zh: 对于这些在21世纪初成长于一个相对自由化国家的年轻女性来说，这并不是回归旧的生活方式。

sentences.en: It was the resurrection of a dark era they knew only through stories passed down from their mothers, accounts of being beaten for dressing improperly
sentences.zh: 这是她们仅从母亲口中讲述的故事里才了解到的黑暗时代的复活，那些因为着装不当

sentences.en: or for leaving the house without a male escort.
sentences.zh: 或没有男性陪同出门而遭到殴打的记录。

sentences.en: When Kabul fell,
sentences.zh: 当喀布尔陷落时，

sentences.en: I felt a part of me was taken,
sentences.zh: “我感觉我的一部分被夺走了，”

sentences.en: Shokriya Saki, who was studying at Brown, told me.
sentences.zh: 在布朗大学学习的舒克里亚·萨基（Shokriya Saki）告诉我。

sentences.en: We thought, this is not the place we have been brought up.
sentences.zh: “我们想，这不是我们长大的地方。”

sentences.en: It's not a country I want to live in, according to the 15th or 16th century.
sentences.zh: “这不是我想居住的国家，这简直是15或16世纪。”

sentences.en: One student told me that one of her father's neighbors had married off a daughter to a Taliban commander.
sentences.zh: 一名学生告诉我，她父亲的一位邻居把女儿嫁给了一名塔利班指挥官。

sentences.en: And when her father went over to the neighbor's house for dinner one night, the Taliban husband was there and confronted her father about his daughters leaving the country.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，当她父亲去邻居家吃晚饭时，那位塔利班丈夫也在场，并质问她父亲关于他女儿们出国的事。

sentences.en: Where are they?
sentences.zh: “她们在哪？”

sentences.en: America?
sentences.zh: “美国？”

sentences.en: Her father lied and told the Taliban that they were married and had moved abroad for their husband's jobs.
sentences.zh: 她父亲撒谎告诉塔利班，她们已经结婚并为了丈夫的工作搬到了国外。

sentences.en: For Hashemi, studying Descartes gave her a new language to navigate her split worlds.
sentences.zh: 对哈希米来说，学习笛卡尔为她提供了一种驾驭分裂世界的语言。

sentences.en: During her meeting with her philosophy teacher to go over the reading, the teacher pulled out a piece of paper and drew a map of Descartes' argument against sensory beliefs.
sentences.zh: 在与哲学老师复习阅读内容的会议中，老师拿出一张纸，画了一张笛卡尔反驳感官信仰的论证图。

sentences.en: She spoke as if she were working through a mathematical equation.
sentences.zh: 她说话的样子就像是在解一道数学题。

sentences.en: So, on the first page, he's saying,
sentences.zh: “所以，在第一页，他说，”

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, everything I might believe may be called into doubt.
sentences.zh: “天哪，我可能相信的一切都可以被怀疑。”

sentences.en: Everything?
sentences.zh: “一切？”

sentences.en: Hashemi asked.
sentences.zh: 哈希米问。

sentences.en: Yeah, everything.
sentences.zh: “是的，一切。”

sentences.en: Remember?
sentences.zh: “记得吗？”

sentences.en: He's sitting in his armchair in his living room and he says,
sentences.zh: “他坐在客厅的扶手椅上，他说，”

sentences.en: I'm going to use the method of skepticism to call everything into doubt.
sentences.zh: “我要用怀疑的方法来质疑一切。”

sentences.en: Even his existence?
sentences.zh: “甚至质疑他的存在？”

sentences.en: Hashemi asked, suppressing a laugh.
sentences.zh: 哈希米忍住笑问道。

sentences.en: Exactly, the teacher said.
sentences.zh: “正是如此，”老师说。

sentences.en: Together, they went through Descartes' method for proving his existence.
sentences.zh: 他们一起梳理了笛卡尔证明其存在的方法。

sentences.en: All we can really know for certain, went his argument, is that we exiSt.
sentences.zh: 他的论点是，我们唯一能确定知道的，就是我们存在。

sentences.en: Does that make sense now?
sentences.zh: “现在明白了吗？”

sentences.en: As we walked back to her dorm room afterward,
sentences.zh: 事后当我们走回她的宿舍时，

sentences.en: Hashemi, still thinking about Descartes, said she believed it was silly for him to question his own existence.
sentences.zh: 哈希米还在思考笛卡尔，她说她认为笛卡尔质疑自己的存在很愚蠢。

sentences.en: But sometimes she, too, felt as if she wasn't sure what was real, here on a snowy campus in Providence, instead of at home with her family in Kabul.
sentences.zh: 但有时她也觉得，自己不确定什么是真实的，是在普罗维登斯白雪皑皑的校园里，还是在喀布尔与家人在一起。

sentences.en: If I close my eyes, I remember the bad things, she told me.
sentences.zh: “如果我闭上眼睛，我就会想起那些糟糕的事情，”她告诉我。

sentences.en: I experienced them.
sentences.zh: “我亲身经历过。”

sentences.en: But still, I feel like it's better to think it was all a bad dream, and it never happened.
sentences.zh: “但即便如此，我觉得最好还是认为那只是一场噩梦，从未发生过。”

sentences.en: Beginning next August, the humanitarian parole will expire for many of the Afghans who fled the country a year ago, potentially stripping them of their access to health care,
sentences.zh: 从明年八月开始，许多一年前逃离阿富汗的人的人道主义假释期将到期，这可能会剥夺他们获得医疗保健、

sentences.en: employment, and the legal right to live in the United States.
sentences.zh: 就业以及在美国居住的合法权利。

sentences.en: While activists have been pressuring Congress to pass an Afghan Adjustment Act, like the 1975
sentences.zh: 虽然活动人士一直在向国会施压，要求通过一项类似于1975年

sentences.en: Vietnamese Refugee Act, that would put the Afghans on a fast track from parole to citizenship, there has been little legislative progress.
sentences.zh: 《越南难民法》的《阿富汗调整法案》，让阿富汗人能够快速从假释过渡到公民身份，但立法进展甚微。

sentences.en: Congress did, however, recently mandate the faster processing of their asylum applications, and until cases are resolved, the applicants can remain in the United States.
sentences.zh: 不过，国会最近确实下令加快处理他们的庇护申请，在案件解决之前，申请人可以留在美国。

sentences.en: The women from AUW have lawyers from several large firms working pro bono on their asylum applications.
sentences.zh: 亚洲女子大学的女性们有来自几家大型律师事务所的律师在为她们的庇护申请提供无偿法律援助。

sentences.en: Since last August,
sentences.zh: 自去年八月以来，

sentences.en: AUW has received about 10,000 applications from young women in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 亚洲女子大学（AUW）已收到约一万份来自阿富汗年轻女性的申请。

sentences.en: Ahmed has already turned his focus to the women still stuck in the country.
sentences.zh: 艾哈迈德已经将目光转向了仍困在阿富汗国内的女性。

sentences.en: In June, he flew from Islamabad to Kabul, where a car from the Taliban waited for him on the airport tarmac.
sentences.zh: 六月，他从伊斯兰堡飞往喀布尔，塔利班的一辆车在机场停机坪上等着他。

sentences.en: As he drove to central Kabul to meet with high-ranking Taliban leaders, the city looked much the same to him as it always had.
sentences.zh: 当他驱车前往喀布尔市中心会见塔利班高层领导人时，这座城市在他眼中看起来和往常没什么两样。

sentences.en: The markets were busy, the traffic was chaotic, but at least one change was visible.
sentences.zh: 市场依然繁忙，交通依然混乱，但至少有一个变化显而易见。

sentences.en: He could see no women on the streets anywhere.
sentences.zh: 他发现街上根本看不到任何女性。

sentences.en: Ahmed told me he went because he wanted to be out in the open with the Taliban about his next project, to enable
sentences.zh: 艾哈迈德告诉我，他此行是因为想公开与塔利班讨论他的下一个项目，即在未来五年内让

sentences.en: 1,000 young women to leave Afghanistan in the next five years so they could continue their studies in Bangladesh.
sentences.zh: 一千名年轻女性离开阿富汗，以便她们能前往孟加拉国继续学业。

sentences.en: His hope was that these women could then help educate younger girls in Afghanistan who have been prevented from attending schools by teaching them online.
sentences.zh: 他希望这些女性之后能通过在线教学，帮助教育阿富汗国内那些被剥夺了受教育权的年轻女孩。

sentences.en: When he proposed the plan to the Taliban over tea and sweets, the immediate response to Ahmed's relief was not no.
sentences.zh: 当他在茶点间隙向塔利班提出这一计划时，令艾哈迈德感到宽慰的是，对方并没有直接拒绝。

sentences.en: It was about logistics, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，对方谈的是后勤问题。

sentences.en: It was not about the central idea of girls' education.
sentences.zh: 这并非针对女孩受教育这一核心理念。

sentences.en: The Taliban told him that a Muharram, a male relative that women, by mandate, must travel with in public, would have to accompany every woman who wanted to attend
sentences.zh: 塔利班告诉他，根据规定，女性在公共场合必须由一名“马哈拉姆”（即男性亲属）陪同，因此每一位想要前往

sentences.en: AUW.
sentences.zh: 亚洲女子大学（AUW）的女性都必须有男性亲属陪同。

sentences.en: The cost was prohibitive for AUW.
sentences.zh: 这对亚洲女子大学来说成本高得令人望而却步。

sentences.en: So now Ahmed is faced with the daunting question,
sentences.zh: 所以现在艾哈迈德面临着一个艰巨的问题：

sentences.en: can he get
sentences.zh: 他能否让

sentences.en: 1,000 women out of the country to study abroad alone?
sentences.zh: 一千名女性独自出国留学？

sentences.en: And even if the women get out, there is no guarantee of stability wherever they land.
sentences.zh: 而且即便她们能离开，无论她们落脚何处，都没有稳定的保障。

sentences.en: In the United States, while a majority of the
sentences.zh: 在美国，虽然大多数

sentences.en: AUW students know what their immediate futures hold,
sentences.zh: 亚洲女子大学的学生清楚自己的近期未来，

sentences.en: ASU,
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那州立大学（ASU）、

sentences.en: Suffolk,
sentences.zh: 萨福克大学、

sentences.en: DePaul, and West Virginia, for example, committed early on to let their students stay until they complete their degrees.
sentences.zh: 德保罗大学和西弗吉尼亚大学等，很早就承诺让学生留校直到完成学位。

sentences.en: Others face more uncertain circumstances.
sentences.zh: 但其他人面临的情况则更为不确定。

sentences.en: At Brown, the women's status as non-degree students was extended through the spring 2023 semester.
sentences.zh: 在布朗大学，这些女性作为非学位生的身份被延长到了2023年春季学期。

sentences.en: Three women who had already completed their undergraduate degrees from
sentences.zh: 三名已经从

sentences.en: AUW have been admitted as full-time traditional master's degree students.
sentences.zh: 亚洲女子大学获得本科学位的女性，已被录取为全日制传统硕士研究生。

sentences.en: But there seems to be confusion among some of the women still pursuing their undergraduate degrees over what might happen next.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些仍在攻读本科学位的女性来说，对于未来会发生什么，似乎存在着困惑。

sentences.en: Hashemi told me that, as far as she knew, she had a spot at
sentences.zh: 哈希米告诉我，据她所知，她今年秋天在

sentences.en: Brown as a degree-earning student this fall.
sentences.zh: 布朗大学有一个攻读学位的名额。

sentences.en: Yet Rowan and Paloma, the associate provosts overseeing the women there, told me that there were no guarantees.
sentences.zh: 然而，负责监管这些女性的副教务长罗文和帕洛玛却告诉我，没有任何保证。

sentences.en: The women who had not yet finished their undergraduate degrees were being encouraged to apply to
sentences.zh: 罗文说，那些尚未完成本科学业的女性被鼓励向

sentences.en: Brown and to apply elsewhere,
